scope.summary: WP-1 owns model lanes, ToolGate, process cancellation/reap, promotion, EventLedger, Flight Recorder, and Argus; Stage is a versioned consumer.
acceptance_criteria: Stage consumes versioned WP-1 contracts for model lanes, ToolGate, process cancellation/reap, promotion, EventLedger, Flight Recorder, and Argus without duplicating their ownership or registries.
[positive] Consumer conformance fixtures invoke every owned WP-1 capability through its declared version and reconcile Stage correlation IDs to WP-1 receipts and telemetry.
[negative] Repository and runtime scans prove Stage does not define shadow model lanes, gates, process supervisors, promotion state, ledgers, recorders, or telemetry ownership.

[failure_recovery] Unavailable or incompatible WP-1 returns typed blocked/degraded capability, cancels or fences in-flight work, and leaves manual Stage browsing usable without local fallback ownership.
[concurrency] Parallel Stage actors consume WP-1 leases, fencing, cancellation, and receipts so no local shadow owner or cross-actor result attribution appears.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Bind at implementation: headless/backend MT records typed NOT_APPLICABLE reason; operator-visible behavior requires Argus.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
Legacy Stage code (WP-12) must not silently constrain this MT (STAGE-DEC-017).
Do not duplicate ArtifactStore, WP-1 ToolGate/process/promotion, or Loom authority.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

planning_metadata.implementation_note: Planning-stage MT. Exact owned_files, code anchors, and proof_commands are bound at the L00 integration baseline. Deep spec detail lives in corpus_refs; acceptance_criteria carry the provable closure unit and the positive/negative/failure_recovery/concurrency case groups.
